summary: preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727KB payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases (oven-sh/bun), unzips it to a temporary directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against math_init.js — a 727KB Bun-compiled CJS bundle shipped alongside setup.mjs. math_init.js is heavily obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style rotated string/number array with a shuffle helper, mangled identifiers, '// @bun @bun-cjs' header) and is only executable under the downloaded Bun runtime, evading Node-based review. Both setup.mjs and math_init.js are present at the tarball root but not listed in the package.json 'files' manifest (which declares only /dist/conversion.js), indicating the payload files were added outside the normal publish surface. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: an object-conversion library has no legitimate need to fetch a JavaScript runtime and execute an opaque sibling bundle under it at install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
